text: The authors state that an important subtask of semi-supervised RL is identifying proxies that predict the reward and learning when they are valid, e.g. a cleaning robot learning that asking 'is the room clean?' or checking for visible dirt approximates a detailed human evaluation. They suggest that semi-supervised RL with a reliable but sparse true approval metric may incentivize communication and transparency, because hiding a mess under the rug breaks the link between the user's reaction and the real reward and so would be avoided.
title: Learning reward proxies; sparse true approval may incentivize agent transparency
